captions.text: By the 6th century BC: Dai stands in northern Hebei.
c. 600 BCE: Anga, easternmost of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, is ruled from Champa.
c. 600 BCE: Asmaka, the only Mahajanapada of the Deccan, is ruled from Potali on the Godavari.
c. 600 BCE: Avanti, ruled from Ujjayini with a southern seat at Mahishmati.
c. 600 BCE: Cedi, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, is ruled from Suktimati in eastern Bundelkhand.
c. 600 BCE: Gandhara, ruled from Taksasila and Puskalavati, holds the Peshawar valley, the Indus crossing and Kashmir.
c. 600 BCE: the Kamboja janapada, one of the Mahajanapadas, holds the cis-Hindukush country from Nuristan to Rajouri, with Rajapura as capital.
c. 600 BCE: Kāśī, capital Vārāṇasī, stands on the map as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.
c. 600 BCE: Kosala, ruled from Shravasti, stands on Awadh as one of the four powers of the north.
c. 600 BCE: the Kuru, a janapada around Indraprastha, stand as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.
c. 600 BCE: Magadha, ruled from Rajagriha, appears as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas on the 'Patna and Gaya districts', bounded by the Ganga, Son and Campā.
c. 600 BCE: the Mallas of Kusinārā and Pāvā stand as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas on the Kushinagar country.
600 BCE: Matsya enters the map as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.
600 BCE: Panchala enters the map as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.
600 BCE: Surasena enters the map as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas on the Yamuna at Mathura.
600 BCE: the Vajjika League stands at Vesali.
600 BCE: Vatsa enters the map as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, with Kausambi as capital.
6th century BC (bridged): the kingdom of Dadan stands at the AlUla oasis.
600 BCE: the sixteen Mahajanapadas stand in the Iron Age north.
c. 600: Phocaean Greeks found Massalia.
6th century: Athens takes Salamis from Megara.
600 BC: Campania.
600: 'Massalia was established c. 600 BC by Ionian Greek settlers from Phocaea'.
Early 6th century BCE: Anga under Dadhivahana overruns Magadha.
c. 600 BCE: Kosala's king Kaṃsa conquers Kāśī for good.
c. 600 BCE: Kaṃsa of Kosala conquers Kāśī.
Early 6th century BCE: Anga and Magadha fight over Magadha.
600: the war with Miletus ends (Lydia infobox '612-600 BC'). 'In 600 BCE, Alyattes resumed his military activities in the west' against Smyrna (Alyattes page).
600: Alyattes takes Smyrna.
The Medes page says the Mannaean states 'probably collapsed', which 'allowed Median groups to take over their territory', without a date; Cliopatria widens the outline in 600.
'a territory stretching roughly from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak River in Anatolia', reached after Assyria's fall; the page gives no year.
c. 600 BCE: the Painted Grey Ware period gives way to the Mahajanapadas.
600 BCE: withdrawal from West Asia.
c. 600 BCE: the court leaves the Kuban for the Dnieper.
the same Elamite outline to the Achaemenid takeover: 'In 540 BC, Achaemenid rule began in Susa'; infobox 'Dates: 3200–539 BC'
the shape unchanged but for -600 only: Kāśī is 'Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE' (infobox); the land passes to janapada-of-kosala

'The country of the Kurus roughly corresponded to the modern Thanesar, state of Delhi, and Meerut district of Uttar Pradesh' (Mahajanapadas page); 'The area formerly occupied by the Kuru Kingdom covered the presently Thanesar, Delhi, and most of the upper Gangetic Doab' (Kuru page); capital Indrapra

shape unchanged for 600-590 apart from the Euphrates strip round Kummuh and Melid (Assyrian-held from 743, as in the 750 and 615 keyframes): valid to 590, the year the Medes 'took over the Urartian capital of Van'; after 590 the land is Median (Cliopatria keeps the Urartu name to 551)

the dossier's Median outline (north-eastern Iran to the Halys, without Afghanistan and Pakistan) without the Urartian kingdom's land, which stays Urartu's until Van falls in 590 (kingdom-of-urartu/ledger/11 then hands it to the Medes)
597 BC: Jerusalem is taken.
c. 591 BC: the capital moves to Meroë.
590: Van falls and Urartu ends.
590: war with the Medes.
589: Nebuchadnezzar returns.
587 BC: Edom rebels against Babylon.
587 BC: Jerusalem is destroyed.
587 BC: Judah becomes Babylonian territory.
586: the tribute ends with the fall of Jerusalem and the annexation of the land as the Babylonian province of Yehud (the loss below).
586: Jerusalem captured.
586: Judah becomes a Babylonian province.
586: the Kingdom of Judah ends.
580s BC: Babylon turns Ammon into a province.
580s BC: Ammon is annexed by Babylon.
580s BC: the Kingdom of Ammon ends as a province of Babylon.
585 BC: Nebuchadnezzar II besieges Tyre.
585: the Battle of the Eclipse ends the Median war.
585 BC: Tarquinius Priscus' Sabine war.

585 BC: Tarquinius Priscus defeats the Sabines: 'Tarquinius returned to Rome and celebrated a triumph on 13 September 585 BC'; 'In the ensuing peace negotiations, the town of Collatia was ceded to Rome'; Corniculum, Ficulea, Cameria, Crustumerium, Ameriola, Medullia and Nomentum 'submitted to Roman administration' (Priscus page); the Roman expansion page: 'Tarquinius Priscus fought the Sabines (in
Rome, the Alban hills, the Tiber mouth and the Sabine-Latin towns of the north-east: the whole kingdom, inside the 15 miles of the Roman expansion page
584: Wu rebels against Chu and annexes the Chu city of Zhoulai.
Cliopatria's 750 shape kept from 584, without the Xu heartland (47 cells), which Xu kept until Wu conquered it in 512
c. 582: Greek colonists from Gela found Akragas.
581: the tyranny ends.
580: Akragas founded ('Thucydides: 580').
574: Shuyong annexed ('Shuyong', 574 BC), another Shu state in central Anhui (researcher's placing; same area as Shuliao).
573 BC: the siege of Tyre ends.
573 BC: Tyre surrenders.
573 BC: Tyre and the Phoenician cities pass under Babylonian rule.
c. 570: Phalaris takes the city.
570: Amasis II conquers Cyprus.
Same year: the Phoenician cells of Cyprus (Kition's area) pass to Egypt in Cliopatria's shapes.
567: Duke Ling of Qi crushes Lai.
567: the state of Lai ends in Qi's conquest; 'The people (Dongyi) were moved to Laiwu.'
565: the first dated Marquess of Yue, Fu Tan, begins his reign at Kuaiji.
560: Heraclea Pontica ('560–550 BC') and Odessa ('About 560 BC').
560 (page undated): Croesus subjugates the mainland Greek cities.
556: Tegea, Sparta's first ally.
553 BC: Nabonidus takes Edom.
c. 553 BC: the Kingdom of Edom ends.
553: Cyrus revolts.
553-550: Cyrus against Astyages.
c. 553 BC: Nabonidus takes Tayma.
c. 552 BC: Nabonidus conquers Dedan and Tayma.
550: Cyrus the Great founds the Achaemenid Empire by defeating the Medes.
Mid-6th century BC: the Messapii of Salento.
550: the Median realm passes to Cyrus.
550 BC: the Po plain to Spina and Adria.
Mid-6th century BCE (undated): Asmaka annexes Mulaka to its west.
550: Cliopatria's Jin shape grows by about 17,000 km2 at Qi's expense.
550: Ecbatana falls.
550: the Medes lose their kingdom.
550: the Median Kingdom ends; the Achaemenid Empire, Cyrus the Great's, begins on its land.
Cliopatria's shape drops 135,554 km2 in -550 (the south-east Turkey and upper Tigris part of the -600 shape).
550: Corinth joins the league ('Corinth joined c. 550'); 'By the 540s, Sparta had alliances with the Peloponnesian cities except Argos and the Achaean cities'.
550: Elis, 'one of the earliest members'.
550: Mantinea in the league.
550: Sicyon in the league.
550: Epidaurus in the league.
550: Phlius in the league.
550: Troezen in the league.
6th century BCE: Qataban under Saba.
550: Cliopatria hands 84 cells of Qi's west (about 17,000 km2) to Jin.
6th century: Qataban under Saba.
550 BCE: Ciscaucasia passes to the Sauromatians.
The dominion of 25 cities.
550: Cliopatria passes one cell to Jin.

Cliopatria's 550 outline without the east and Susiana: the campaigns in the east ran 'between around 545 BC to 540 BC' and 'By the year 540 BC, Cyrus captured Elam and its capital, Susa' (Cyrus the Great); the Median realm that Cyrus took in 550 ran 'from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak River' (Medes).

the shape as drawn (Laconia and Messenia excluded by Cliopatria already), for -550..-548 without the mainland Ionian and Aeolian coast: Croesus (reign c. 560-546) 'subjugated all of mainland Ionia, Aeolis, and Doris' while he 'abandoned his plans of annexing the Greek city-states on the islands of t

18,961 km2 for 550-501, Lower Macedonia under Alcetas and Amyntas I. Persian vassal from 512/511 (infobox 'Vassal of Persia: 512/511-493 BC'), so the last decade of this shape is vassal tint under the achaemenid-empire dossier.
569,654 km2 (-550..-541), ratio 1.14 against the infobox's 500,000 km2 for 562.

the shape as drawn: Laconia and Messenia (Lacedaemon) are Sparta's own land; the Tegean (Arcadian) and Corinthian cells inside the shape are allies of the league that 'evolved into the Peloponnesian League' and are drawn as Sparta's tint, not its colour
Cliopatria's 550 Saba shape plus Qataban's Wadi Bayhan land, which came under Saba in the 6th century
0.64 M km2 between the Dniester and the Don-Volga: right.

Shape unchanged, years only: Egypt plus Cyprus holds -570..-546 ('In 570 BC, Cyprus was conquered by Egypt under Amasis II'; 'Egyptian rule lasted for about 25 years until 545 BC'); Cliopatria has it -550..-531
6,909 km2 for -550..-451: one cell passes to Jin at 550.
547: Cyrus takes Ionia.
547: Croesus crosses the Halys.
the -540 shape: the aggregate without Ionia and Aeolis, Persian from 547 | corrected: less Syracuse and its chora, which the syracuse dossier holds from 733
546: Cyrus conquers Lydia.
546: 'Commagene was incorporated into Persia in 546 BC.' The page names no previous ruler.
546: Argos loses Thyreatis to Sparta after the Battle of the 300 Champions ('roughly 546 BC').
546: Sardis falls to Cyrus.
546: the whole kingdom passes to Persia.
546: Lydia ends.
546: Thyrea won from Argos.
545: Cyprus passes to Persia.
544: Bimbisara founds the Haryanka dynasty at Rajagriha.
543 BCE: Prince Vijaya lands in Lanka and founds the Kingdom of Tambapanni.
543 BCE: Bimbisara takes the Magadhan throne and Magadha is Anga's no longer.
543 BCE: Bimbisara takes the Magadhan throne ('r.
543 BC: Nabonidus leaves Tayma.
c. 543 BC (bridged): the Lihyanite kingdom replaces the Dadanite.
542: Harpagus completes the conquest of Asia Minor.
Page silent: the Cyrus the Great page does not mention Cilicia, but Cliopatria's 540 outline holds it (87 percent) and the page has Harpagus 'finish the conquest of Asia Minor' in 542.
540: Cyrus takes Elam and Susa.
540: Cyrus' eastern campaigns end.
540 BC: Corsica.
540-535: Alalia.
3.71 M km2: Lydia, Ionia, Caria, Lycia, Cilicia (Turkey 92 percent), the east and Susiana are in, Babylonia (539) and Egypt are not.

the -530 shape (Po valley, Etruria and Corsica) plus Etruria, Capua and the Campanian plain of the -600 shape west of the Tiber, the Veii country and the Caere-Pyrgi coast: Corsica from the battle of Alalia (540-535)
539 BCE: the Persians organise Yehud as a province.
Page undated: 'By 525 BC, Cambyses had successfully subjugated Phoenicia and Cyprus', and the Phoenician fleet made up 'a large part of Cambyses' fleet'.
539 BCE: Elam ends in the Persian empire.
539 BC (bridged): Babylon falls to Cyrus.
539 BC (bridged): Moab passes to Persia.
539 BC: Cyrus the Great takes Babylon and the Levant becomes one satrapy.
539 BC: the Phoenician city-states pass under Persian rule.
539 BC: Babylonian rule ends when Cyrus takes Babylon.
539 BC: Qedar enters the Achaemenid Empire.

539 BCE: Yehud is one of 'twenty provinces or administrative subunits in the large satrapy of Eber-nari'; the Achaemenid governors (Sheshbazzar appointed 538) rule it, so it is drawn as the Achaemenid Empire's tinted dependency, not as sovereign land.
539: Cyrus takes Babylon.
539 BC (bridged): Tyre's tie ends with the empire.
12 Oct.
538: Lai annexed ('Lai (賴國)', 538 BC). Location not given; placed on the upper Huai near Xi County, confidence 1.
By 538 Chu holds Zhongli.
By 538 the state of Zhongli has ended in Chu's conquest; the year is a bound, not a date.
c. 535 BCE: Cyrus makes Gandhara a Persian satrapy.
c. 535 BCE: Cyrus the Great annexes Gandhara west of the Indus.
534 BC: first appearance.
534: King Ling of Chu makes Chen a prefecture.
534: King Ling annexes Chen.
531: King Ling of Chu seizes Cai.
531: the seat moves to Xincai.
531: King Ling annexes Cai.
c. 530 BCE: Bimbisara of Magadha kills Brahmadatta and annexes Anga; Champa becomes a viceroy's seat.
c. 530 BCE: Cyrus destroys the Kamboja city of Kapisi (Begram).
c. 530 BCE: Bimbisara annexes Anga.
c. 530 BCE: the stretch of the Ganga's south bank between the Patna-Gaya core and the annexed Anga country is drawn as Magadha's.
4.27 M km2: Mesopotamia and the Levant are in (Cliopatria books them from 530, nine years after October 539), Egypt and Cyprus are not.

Magadha with Anga after Bimbisara's annexation: 'Anga was annexed by Magadha in the time of Bimbisara'; the Patna-Gaya core, the Ganga-bank stretch to the Campā border, and the Anga country (Anga disc plus Bhagalpur 60 km)
529: Cai restored at Xincai.
529: Chen restored.
529: Chen restored after King Ling's fall.
529: Cai restored at Xincai.
525 or before: Cyprus passes to Persia.
525: 'In 525 BC, after conquering Egypt, the Achaemenid (Persian) army of Cambyses II seized the Pentapolis' (Cyrenaica page).
525: the cities of the Pentapolis appear as one unit.
525: the Persians seize the Pentapolis.
525: Cyrenaica passes to Persia.
525 BC: Cambyses II conquers Egypt.
525 BC: the Saite Dynasty ends with the Persian conquest.
525: Cambyses II wins Egypt at Pelusium and the Twenty-seventh Dynasty begins.
525: Cambyses II conquers Egypt.
525: Egypt is held by the Persian kings as the First Egyptian Satrapy (525-404).
519: Megara 'possibly joined c. 519 BCE'.
518 BCE: Darius conquers Sindhu-Sauvira and organises it as the satrapy of Hindush.
518 BCE: Taxila and the Indus-Jhelum country join Hindush (the Hindush page has c. 513 BCE for the conquest).
c. 518 BCE: Darius I's army reaches the Jhelum; Taksasila falls and Gandhara ends as a kingdom.
518 BCE: Darius I conquers Sindhu-Sauvira and makes it the satrapy of Hindush.

'the lower and central Indus basin' / 'present-day Sindh and the southern Punjab in Pakistan' (Hindush page): Sindh and the Multan country together with Taxila and the land between the Indus and the Jhelum, which the conquest page makes Hindush's capital district ('Bhir Mound in Takshashila') with '
515: Darius I conquers the Indus.
Gedrosia (Makran, 'from the Indus River to the north-eastern edge of the Strait of Hormuz') 'was conquered by Cyrus the Great or Darius the Great'; the page gives no year.
513: Thrace becomes Persian.
512: Macedonia submits.
512: Xu annexed ('Xu', 512 BC). Cliopatria keeps an Xu row to 285, which this contradicts; the region is Xu's Cliopatria shape.
512/511: Macedon a vassal of Persia.

512: Wu conquers Xu. Xu page: 'Reduced to its heartland, Xu was eventually conquered by Wu in 512 BC'; infobox 'Conquered by Wu: 512 BC'; the Spring and Autumn table 'Xu 512 BCE: to Wu'. The Chu dossier also claims Xu for 512, from the Chu page.
512: Wu conquers Xu and the state ends.
510: Croton destroys Sybaris and heads its region.
510: Kroton destroys Sybaris.
510: the end of Sybaris.
509 BC: the Tarquins expelled; Brutus and Collatinus the first consuls.

509 BC: 'Monarchy overthrown: 509 BC'. After Lucretia's death 'Lucius Junius Brutus led a revolt' that 'deposed and expelled Tarquinius and his family from Rome in 509 BC'; Brutus and Collatinus 'became Rome's first consuls, marking the beginning of the Roman Republic'.
508: Cleisthenes establishes Athenian democracy.
506: Wu takes Ying.
506: King Helü invades Chu and Wu takes the Chu capital Ying.
506 BC: the Xianyu found Zhongshan at Tang County.
506 BC: the state is Zhongshan in the record.
505: Chu recovers Ying.
c. 505 BCE: the seat moves north to Upatissagama.
505: Qin and Chu drive Wu out of Ying.
504: the court moves briefly to Ruo.

505-504 BC: 'there was war between republican Rome and the Sabines'; Publius Valerius Poplicola 'celebrated a triumph over both the Sabines and the Veientes in May 504 BC'. The page does not say where; the disc north of Rome is my reading.
May 504 BC: the triumph ends the war.
c. 501 BCE: Kamboja is absorbed into the Achaemenid Empire.
501 BCE: the Janapada of Magadha row ends and Cliopatria's Haryanka row (33,403 km2, from -500) takes the same land.
